details.claim: The change deliberately generates a formatter for a type from a referenced assembly in the consuming assembly. This looks like it conflicts with TypeCollector's metadata-only early return, but the new path is a separate collector driven by the explicit attribute, so it is consistent with the requirement.
cited_entries: [L11] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367)
details.plan: [L11] Referenced-assembly types are not auto-formatted by TypeCollector.CollectCore, but REQ-2129 explicitly opts in via [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter].
